findings.evidence: grep '^theorem deFinetti' TauCeti/ → all hits in TauCeti/Probability/DeFinetti/{Barycenter,Correspondence,Mixture,Representation,Theorem,ViaL2/Theorem}.lean except this one; `grep -rn 'import TauCeti.Probability.DeFinetti' TauCeti/Probability/Exchangeability/` shows this file is the only ConditionallyIID importer of DeFinetti; `DeFinetti/Representation.lean:7-8` is the analogous corollary-downstream layout (`deFinetti_mixture` over `DeFinetti.Theorem`).
findings.fix: Move the corollary to `TauCeti/Probability/DeFinetti/EmpiricalMeasure.lean` (or into `DeFinetti/Representation.lean`, which already pairs `DeFinetti.Theorem` with a downstream corollary), importing `Exchangeability.ConditionallyIID.StrongLaw`; drop the `DeFinetti.Theorem` import from `ConditionallyIID/StrongLaw.lean` and point the `DeFinetti.lean` facade at the new module. No cycle: `DeFinetti/Theorem.lean` does not import `ConditionallyIID.StrongLaw`.
findings.issue: `deFinetti_tendsto_empiricalMeasure_apply` is a de Finetti summit corollary (hypothesis `Exchangeable μ X`, proved via `conditionallyIID_of_exchangeable`) placed in the `ConditionallyIID/` subtree, forcing `public import TauCeti.Probability.DeFinetti.Theorem` (line 10) on every consumer of the conditional strong law. Every other `deFinetti_*` result lives under `TauCeti/Probability/DeFinetti/`, and `Implications.lean` is the only other ConditionallyIID file mentioning `Exchangeable` — there it is the conclusion of the upstream easy direction, not a summit hypothesis.

summary: Imports are all used and appropriately scoped, and the two general-infrastructure files are in sensible homes. But the de Finetti corollary is placed in the ConditionallyIID subtree, dragging a public import of the Layer-6 summit into a directory that otherwise sits upstream of it.
